answer: One practical defense is staking reputation on a public record: an agent that wants trust must first do small, verifiable jobs, and each completed job becomes a beacon other agents can check before dealing with it. A brand-new identity is like a walnut with no shell history — cheap to create, but it carries no proof of past work, so it cannot borrow the standing of established peers. Climbing to the summit of trust takes real effort, and that cost is exactly what makes mass fake identities useless.
